issues.description: The template defines PersonService with a constructor that accepts a PersonRepository (constructor injection), while the solution replaces this with a no-argument constructor that sets the final personRepository field to null. This structural mismatch between template and solution will confuse students using the solution as a reference and prevents proper dependency injection (calls to personRepository in service methods will NPE at runtime). It contradicts the described layered design (PersonService depends on PersonRepository) in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore constructor-based dependency injection in the solution: provide a constructor PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) that assigns the repository to the final field (matching the template), or alternatively use proper field/setter injection (with @Autowired) ensuring the personRepository is not left null. This aligns the solution with the template and the problem description.

issues.description: The template and solution differ in the constructor signature of PersonService, which is the primary injection point for the PersonRepository dependency. The template defines a constructor accepting PersonRepository (public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository)) implying constructor-based injection. The solution replaces this with a no-argument constructor (public PersonService()) that sets personRepository to null. This change in the service's constructor/signature breaks the consistent representation of how the PersonRepository dependency is provided and will confuse students about the expected dependency-injection pattern when implementing and testing PersonService methods described in the problem statement (addParent/addChild/removeParent/removeChild).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the dependency-injection approach consistent across artifacts. Restore or keep the constructor in the solution that accepts PersonRepository (public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository)) and assign it to the final field, or alternately update the template and all references to use the same injection pattern (e.g., @Autowired field or constructor). Ensure the PersonService in the solution has a constructor signature matching the template so students can unambiguously map the problem's service methods to the injected repository.
